framework: Spring Cloud Config native + Consul + Spring Boot Admin
cicdPlatform: None — no .github, GitLab CI, Jenkinsfile, Azure Pipeline, CircleCI or other pipeline definition exists
containerization: Single-stage Dockerfiles only for person-service and user-service; both require a pre-built jar, expose a fictional 8080 while services use random ports, and there is no Docker Compose file
orchestration: None — no Kubernetes manifests, Helm chart, Terraform or other deployment definition
deploymentStrategy: Manual local runtime: start Consul, MySQL and config-service, then start Spring Boot jars; service discovery resolves random ports. No automated deployment or promotion path exists.
monitoringStack: Spring Boot Admin UI + Actuator + rolling file logs; no Prometheus, Micrometer registry, centralized logging or alerting

environments.name: dev-local
environments.configurationSource: config-service classpath:/config/ plus local module configuration
environments.notes: This is the only environment expressible by the repository.

integrations.name: HashiCorp Consul
integrations.risk: register-health-check is false in every delivered service, and Consul never evicts a dead instance

integrations.name: MySQL
integrations.risk: No compose file; Hibernate ddl-auto:update owns schema history and plaintext credentials are delivered through config-service

integrations.name: Gmail SMTP
integrations.risk: plaintext username and app password, no timeout/retry/idempotency, no fallback provider

integrations.name: Spring Cloud Config
integrations.risk: unauthenticated, only 4 of 8 services consume it, and the git backend block remains committed but inactive

integrations.name: Spring Boot Admin
integrations.risk: admin UI binds all interfaces, uses one committed credential pair, and admin-service is not monitored itself

integrations.name: GitHub config-repo
integrations.risk: The SSH block and deploy-key material are still committed while README describes it as active

integrations.name: Kafka
integrations.risk: No spring-kafka dependency exists in any pom; do not describe the platform as event-driven

patterns: Config-service uses the native Spring Cloud Config backend and serves checked-in classpath:/config/ YAML files; no git fetch occurs at runtime
Fixed ports are reserved for infrastructure and edge components; business services mostly use server.port: 0 and Consul-assigned ephemeral ports
Gateway route definitions are authored in config-service, not gateway-service; discovery.locator.enabled makes the three explicit routes a convenience list rather than an allow-list
All four delivered service documents expose every actuator endpoint with include "*"
Logback file rolling is configured in every service, but four delivered documents use the deprecated logging.file.max-size and max-history keys
Consul host/port are hardcoded to localhost:8500 with no environment override
A Maven wrapper is committed in every module at Maven 3.8.6 / wrapper 3.1.0
conventions: Spring application name determines Consul service id and the native config-service document name
Configuration is currently local for auth-service, admin-service, account-service and config-service; central for gateway, notification, person and user
Environment overrides use ${NAME:default} for CONFIG_SERVER, ADMIN_SERVER and APP_JWT_SECRET
Runtime logs are written under the working directory logs/ and must be added to .gitignore rather than tracked
constraints: P0 — secrets are committed and pushed to a public GitHub repository; externalization and history remediation are user-owned and not started
There is no staging or production deployment target, environment, secret store, CI runner or release process
No container base images, health checks, resource limits, reverse proxy, ingress or secret mounting are defined
Consul and MySQL are manual local prerequisites
account-service cannot start as committed because it has JPA but no datasource, no Consul dependency and no config-service document
Committed runtime logs may contain resolved secrets, but this is unverified
Do not expose any service port as a stable public contract without narrowing actuator exposure and adding authentication/authorization
projectSpecificNotes: Phase 4 found 7 deployable services plus 1 scaffold; 4 central configuration consumers, 4 local consumers; 2 Dockerfiles, 0 Compose, 0 orchestrator, 0 CI/CD and 0 real staging/production definitions. The infrastructure surface is local-first and not deployable as a cohesive platform.
